verdict.honest_reading: On fresh MIXED-CAUSAL-v3 the frozen v3.1 policy scored highest overall (99/180 vs best constant 97), with one regression and lower cost than the constants it edged. But the +2-success margin over ALWAYS_CONSTRAINED is not statistically distinguishable from zero (CI spans zero), and it does NOT significantly beat the best simple rule either. Per-family analysis is worse than the aggregate: on selection and realization tasks - where interventions matter most - the policy UNDERPERFORMED the corresponding constants by wide margins. Its aggregate lead comes mostly from copy_single parity and reduced intervention waste on no_intervention tasks.
scope_limits: composition unsolvable under current action set (structural)
non_candidate open-answer verification weak (all arms tie)
single fixture; second fresh draw would strengthen any future claim

next_research_question: Why does the policy underperform its own per-action predictors' implied choices on selection/realization families — is the utility rule's cost term mis-calibrated, or do the per-action success models fail to transfer across fixtures?
